notes: Conference slide deck (ICARDA/FAO, 2019) on rehabilitation of a degraded silvopastoral rangeland at the Sbaihia pilot site, Zaghouan, Tunisia: planting of carob, tree medic, old man saltbush (in micro-catchments), cactus and agave, sulla (Hedysarum coronarium) reseeding, gabions and manual benches (water harvesting, out of scope). The only economic values are daily feed costs per head on slide 18 (p18). Not extracted: seedling survival rates (p16, figure), sulla DM yield (p19, figure), trainees 405/294/111 (p22, not adoption), expected soil and water retention (p20-21). Slide 18 states a 'high adoption rate for sulla reseeding' but gives no number. Practice fit is uncertain: the cost value belongs to the sulla-reseeded pasture component of the silvopastoral rehabilitation, not to the trees/shrubs; coded silvopasture with that caveat (alternatives: feed_mgmt planted forage, or improved pasture sowing = partial_bundle under rotational_grazing). Grey literature (slides): no methods for how the feed costs were estimated.
